names.official: Personal income tax on employment and similar income ("tax on payroll and workforce")
names.native: Gyventojų pajamų mokestis (darbo jėgos ir atlyginimo mokesčiai)

taxes.base: Wages and similar employment income; withheld by the employer.

rate.headline: 20% · 32% (also 5% · 15% on certain income)
details: 2024 rates: 5%, 15%, 20% and 32%; basic exemption up to EUR 747 a month (EUR 8,964 a year) if pay does not exceed the minimum wage of EUR 924.
Rate from the Grant Thornton Baltic summary for 2024; not checked against the State Tax Inspectorate, whose site refused automated access.

instruments.explanation: The largest direct tax and the biggest line after VAT. Eurostat’s accounts book all of the personal income tax under central government.

legalRefs.locator: Key Lithuanian tax rates; PIT law changes from 1 January 2024

names.official: Personal income tax on income from individual activities

taxes.base: Income of self-employed people from individual activity.

rate.headline: Personal income tax rates
details: The National Tax List gives it its own line; revenue fell from EUR 193.8 million in 2023 to EUR 163.7 million in 2024.

instruments.explanation: The tax on the self-employed, separate from the tax withheld on wages.

names.official: Personal income tax on capital income

taxes.base: Dividends, interest, rents, and gains from the sale of assets of individuals.

details: The National Tax List shows EUR 651.2 million in 2024 against EUR 600.4 million in 2023. The exact rates by type of income are in the Law on Personal Income Tax and are not itemised here.

instruments.explanation: The part of the personal income tax that falls on returns to capital.

names.official: Corporate profit tax

taxes.base: Profit of companies and other legal persons.

rate.headline: 15% standard; 20% for credit institutions
details: 2024 rates: 15% standard, 20% for credit institutions, reduced rates of 5% and 0%.
Rate from the Grant Thornton Baltic summary for 2024; not checked against the State Tax Inspectorate, whose site refused automated access.

instruments.explanation: The corporate income tax. Revenue was EUR 1.78 billion in 2024, slightly more than in 2023.

names.official: Temporary bank solidarity tax

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: a temporary tax on banks; the list gives no more detail.

rate.headline: Temporary; set by law
details: EUR 219.9 million in 2024 and EUR 249.8 million in 2023 in the list.

instruments.explanation: A temporary levy on the banking sector that the list books with the corporate income tax.

names.official: Social insurance contributions paid by households (employees and the self-employed)
names.native: Valstybinio socialinio draudimo ir privalomojo sveikatos draudimo įmokos (gyventojų)

taxes.base: Gross pay and the income of the self-employed. The National Tax List gives this line only as the subtotal "households’ actual social contributions".
taxes.payer: Employees (withheld by the employer) and the self-employed.

rate.headline: 19.5% of gross pay (employee)
details: The 2024 rate on the employee’s pay is 19.5%, withheld; the employer pays 1.77% on top.
Rate from the Grant Thornton Baltic summary for 2024; not checked against the State Tax Inspectorate, whose site refused automated access.

instruments.explanation: Since the 2019 reform nearly all of the contributions are paid by employees, so this line is the big one; the list shows only EUR 629 million for employers. Collected by the State Tax Inspectorate and paid to Sodra, the social insurance fund.

names.official: Social insurance contributions paid by employers

taxes.base: Gross pay. The National Tax List gives this line only as the subtotal "employers’ actual social contributions".

rate.headline: 1.77% of gross pay on top
details: 2024 rate of the employer’s contribution, per the Grant Thornton summary.
Rate from the Grant Thornton Baltic summary for 2024; not checked against the State Tax Inspectorate, whose site refused automated access.

instruments.explanation: A small line since the 2019 reform moved most contributions to the employee.

names.official: Value added tax

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Lithuania, intra-EU acquisitions and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 21% standard; 9% and 5% reduced
details: 2024: standard rate 21%; the 9% rate was abolished for restaurant and catering services at the end of 2023. Registration threshold EUR 45,000.
Rate from the Grant Thornton Baltic summary for 2024; not checked against the State Tax Inspectorate, whose site refused automated access.

instruments.explanation: The largest single tax, at about 8% of GDP.

names.official: Taxes on international trade and transactions (customs duties)

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions.

instruments.explanation: Collected by customs for the EU budget.

names.official: Excise duty on oil products and on electricity
names.native: Akcizai už naftos produktus ir elektros energiją

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel and other oil products, and electricity, by quantity.
taxes.payer: Producers, importers and suppliers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per unit of quantity, fixed by the Law on Excise Duties
details: EUR 1,056.5 million on oil products, EUR 1.2 million on oil-product imports and EUR 2.5 million on electricity in 2024.

instruments.explanation: The biggest excise.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D214A C05 and C06, D2122C C03

names.official: Excise duty on manufactured tobacco

taxes.base: Cigarettes and other manufactured tobacco.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Fixed by the Law on Excise Duties
details: EUR 409.4 million on domestic and intra-EU tobacco and EUR 10.4 million on imports in 2024.

instruments.explanation: The second largest excise.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D214A C04, D2122C C02

names.official: Excise duty on alcoholic beverages (wine, beer and other alcohol)

taxes.base: Wine, beer and other alcoholic beverages (mainly spirits), by volume or pure alcohol.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per litre, fixed by the Law on Excise Duties
details: EUR 316.7 million on other alcoholic beverages, EUR 119.3 million on beer, EUR 68.0 million on wine and EUR 6.3 million on alcohol imports in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Other alcoholic beverages (spirits) bring in most of it.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D214A C01 to C03, D2122C C01

names.official: Tax on lotteries and gambling

taxes.base: Gambling and lottery operators’ takings.

rate.headline: Set by the Law on Gaming
details: EUR 73.9 million in 2024 and EUR 67.0 million in 2023 in the list.

instruments.explanation: The gambling tax.

names.official: Car and motor vehicle registration taxes and conveyance (vehicle) taxes
names.native: Automobilių ir motorinių transporto priemonių registracijos mokesčiai; transporto priemonių mokesčiai

taxes.base: The registration of cars and motor vehicles; conveyances.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: EUR 37.1 million motor vehicle registration tax, EUR 19.1 million car registration taxes and EUR 23.0 million conveyance taxes in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Three lines of the list that tax the owning and registering of vehicles.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D214D C01 and C02, D29B C01

names.official: Pollution taxes and Modernisation Fund taxes
names.native: Mokestis už aplinkos teršimą; Modernizavimo fondo mokesčiai

taxes.base: Emissions and pollution; the Modernisation Fund line is named in the list without further detail.

rate.headline: Set by the Law on Pollution Tax
details: EUR 52.2 million pollution tax and EUR 55.4 million Modernisation Fund taxes in 2024. The sale of emission permits (EUR 113.7 million) is not counted.

instruments.explanation: Eurostat records EUR 17 million of the pollution taxes with local government; the list does not say which line.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D29F C01 and C02

names.official: Deductions from revenue under the Forestry Law
names.native: Atskaitymai nuo pajamų pagal Miškų įstatymą

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: deductions from revenue under the Republic of Lithuania Forestry Law; no further detail.

rate.headline: Set by the Forestry Law
details: EUR 44.0 million in 2024 and EUR 49.7 million in 2023.

instruments.explanation: Booked by the statisticians as a tax on products.

names.official: Deposit and investment insurance tax, Resolution Fund contributions and health care institutions’ contributions
names.native: Indėlių ir investicijų draudimo mokestis; įmokos į Pertvarkymo fondą; sveikatos priežiūros įstaigų įmokos

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List; no further detail.
taxes.payer: Financial institutions and health care institutions.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: EUR 48.5 million deposit and investment insurance tax, EUR 7.8 million health care institutions’ contributions in 2024; the Resolution Fund line is zero in 2024 (EUR 6.1 million in 2023).

instruments.explanation: Compulsory contributions that the statisticians book as taxes on production.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D29E C02 to C04

names.official: Other taxes on production, State fees and registration taxes, other taxes on products and households’ licence payments
names.native: Kiti gamybos mokesčiai; valstybės rinkliavos; registracijos mokesčiai; kiti mokesčiai gaminiams; licencijų mokėjimai

taxes.base: The list’s residual lines: other taxes on production n.e.c. (EUR 57.5 million), registration taxes (EUR 29.5 million), State-imposed fees and charges (EUR 9.8 million), other taxes on products (EUR 1.7 million) and households’ licence payments (EUR 3.3 million).

rate.headline: Various
details: Eurostat’s accounts record EUR 34 million of the "other taxes on production" with local government; the list does not say which.

instruments.explanation: Five lines that the list does not break down further.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D29H C01, D214B, D214C, D214H, D59D

names.official: Immovable property tax

taxes.base: The value of immovable property (buildings, premises) of companies and some individuals.

rate.headline: Set by each municipality within limits
details: The Law on Immovable Property Tax lets each municipality set the rate within a legal range; the planned 2024 reform to widen the tax was put on hold (Grant Thornton).

instruments.explanation: The main tax of Lithuania’s municipalities and the largest of their taxes.

names.official: Land tax (companies and households)

taxes.base: The value of land; the list separates the tax paid by corporations (EUR 26.4 million) from households (EUR 50.5 million).

rate.headline: Set by each municipality within limits
details: The list does not give rates. Eurostat records EUR 34 million of the households’ land tax with local government and EUR 16 million with central government.

instruments.explanation: The second municipal property tax.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LT, D29A C01, D59A C01

names.official: Inheritance tax

taxes.base: Inherited property.

rate.headline: Set by the Law on Inheritance Tax
details: EUR 4.3 million in 2024; Eurostat records the capital taxes with local government.

instruments.explanation: The only wealth transfer tax; tiny.
